drafted_from: tool:put-records-into-my-account row (tools/export-records-as-list-rows/what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json), read-data/record_write_plan.py, do-work/plan_record_write.py and test/test_record_write_plan.py; the answer is what do-work/plan_record_write.py printed on the made-up input below
start_here: Say to your AI: "Put the records I built into my account, and tell me what you wrote and whether my account matches."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it works out the writes from the payload the builder made and the records your own store holds, and writes nothing. Your store is written and read by your AI directly, in its own language.
instructions: 1. Build the payload with tool:build-records-to-write (see its kit) and keep the result object.
2. Read the target records your store holds now, the one record type and id prefix the payload's records use, straight from your own store, as { id, type, value } records.
3. Say "Plan the writes"; your AI runs tool:put-records-into-my-account with mode plan, the payload, target_type, target_prefix, held and config { per_command, command_bytes, request_key_prefix }.

4. Write each command in the answer into your store yourself: set each record's value, or remove it when value is null. A record that carries expected must find exactly that value (or none) when you write it; refuse and stop when it does not.

5. Read the target records back from your store and run the tool with mode readback. all_equal means the store matches the payload; readback_differs names the records missing or different, and conflicts name a live edit that was kept on purpose.

worked_examples.title: One row is new and one holds an old title, so two records are planned
worked_examples.ask: Put the records I built into my account.
worked_examples.given: Read from a real run of do-work/plan_record_write.py on made-up input (the same input as the mcp example, on standard input). The payload holds two sample-row records and one other record; the store holds sample-list:row-2 with an old title and no sample-list:row-1.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"state": "to_write", "records": 2, "to_write": 2, "commands": [{"input": {"records": [{"id": "sample-list:row-1", "type": "sample-row", "value": {"title": "Sample row"}}, {"id": "sample-list:row-2", "type": "sample-row", "value": {"title": "Second row"}}]}, "request_key": "sample-load-e0841c1061f3c72c64167cafbe01dde9"}], "out_of_scope": 1} Then the AI writes both records of the one command into the store, and calls again with mode readback; the store matching the payload gives state all_equal and exit 0.
